why: Doc sentence is verbatim (w14.md:132, single-sentence <div> in the 'Other wins' digest grid, no second clause reversing it). The IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: no `showThinkingSummaries` exists in our source or settings schema, and the cited lines check out with minor drift (storage.ts:56 `defaultThinkingLevel`, storage.ts:189 workspaceDefaults `thinkingLevel: 'medium'`; the claim said :55/:184). The 'grep -> 0 files' evidence is also defensible on a clean checkout: `grep -ra` over packages/apps/scripts/docs actually returns 5 code files, but all are UNTRACKED build outputs (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/{dist/,}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js) that bundle @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, plus this sweep's own doc rows; `git ls-files --error-unmatch` rejects all three. So the identifier survives. The CONSEQUENCE does not, on three independent counts. (1) The default posture is the SAME, not opposite. `type: 'thinking'` renders only inside the turn's activity section, which is collapsed by default: the live chat passes a controlled `isExpanded` from `useTurnCardExpansion` initialized to an empty Set (apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useTurnCardExpansion.ts:59-64), TurnCard's own fallback is `defaultExpanded = false` (packages/ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:2780, mirrored at SessionViewer.tsx:81), and the collapsed header preview surfaces `intent`, `intermediate` content and running tool names but never `thinking` content (getPreviewText, TurnCard.tsx:721-753). 'Claude now hides them by default, we always show them' is therefore false: we hide them by default too, and the user's expand choice persists per session in localStorage. (2) A user AND admin control over whether thinking appears at all does exist: `thinkingLevel: 'off'`, the first entry of THINKING_LEVEL_IDS (packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:28), carried in the UI dropdown metadata THINKING_LEVELS, validated (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:130), settable app-level (`defaultThinkingLevel`, storage.ts:56/2483-2499) and workspace-level (storage.ts:189). It maps to THINKING_TO_EFFORT.off = null -> `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }` (claude-agent.ts:247) with a 0 token budget, so no thinking is produced and none can appear. 'No user or admin control over whether they appear at all' is simply wrong. (3) Enforcement one layer up on the only backend where Claude's key is meaningful: claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']`, so the bundled SDK reads the user's ~/.claude/settings.json, and `showThinkingSummaries` is a first-class key in that SDK's own settings schema (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:5915, 'Request API-side thinking summaries and show them in the conversation and in the transcript view (ctrl+o)'). This is the exact false-positive shape AGENTS.md and inert-worklist section 4 item 3 name: the identifier is absent from our schema, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handles it. Surface mismatch compounds it: 'thinking summaries' is the Anthropic-API summarized-thinking feature and 'interactive sessions' is Claude Code's TUI-vs-`-p` distinction, while Nessy Desktop is a GUI with no `-p` mode whose primary backend is the Nestor OpenAI-like gateway. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (checked; none concern thinking).
correctedState: No `showThinkingSummaries` key exists in Nessy's own settings schema — correct — but the claimed changed-default divergence is not real. Thinking renders only inside the turn's activity section, which is COLLAPSED BY DEFAULT (useTurnCardExpansion.ts:59-64 initializes to an empty Set; TurnCard.tsx:2780 `defaultExpanded = false`), and the collapsed preview never surfaces thinking content (TurnCard.tsx:721-753), so our default posture matches Claude's new one rather than opposing it. A control over whether thinking appears at all also exists: `thinkingLevel: 'off'` (thinking-levels.ts:28, validators.ts:130), settable per session, per workspace (storage.ts:189) and app-wide (`defaultThinkingLevel`, storage.ts:56), which disables thinking entirely (claude-agent.ts:247, 0 token budget). On the Claude backend the key itself is already honored upstream: claude-agent.ts:305 sets `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so the bundled Claude Agent SDK reads `showThinkingSummaries` from the user's ~/.claude/settings.json (sdk.d.ts:5915). The only honest residual is a nuance, not a divergence: Nessy has no display-only toggle that keeps reasoning effort high while suppressing the summary text — the nearest controls are suppress-entirely (`thinkingLevel: 'off'`) and hide-by-default collapse.
